text:
A: Hello! Hi, there we go. How's your day going?
B: Alright. Knackered.
A: I bet. I'm Gareth.
B: Kayleigh.
A: Nice to meet you, Kayleigh. Have you been on shift? I spotted the lanyard in your photo.
B: Yeah. Care home. Twelve hours. I'm only doing this for the money, to be fair.
A: Ha, honest. I respect that. I'm a teacher, geography, down in Maidstone. And Head of Year 9, so I spend most of my life sorting out arguments about who said what on TikTok.
B: TikTok's where all the arguments are. I'm on there every night arguing in the comments.
A: Are you? Go on then, what about?
B: Local Facebook stuff mainly. Somebody'll moan about the carnival traffic and I'll go off.
A: Carnival? Where are you?
B: Bridgwater. Somerset. We've got the biggest carnival, November, all lit up. The carts are massive, they spend all year building them.
A: Oh, the illuminated one! I've seen that on telly. That looks brilliant.
B: It is. People who moan about the roads being shut can do one, honestly. It's one night. I'm not being funny but it's the best thing about Bridgwater.
A: No, fair enough. You're proud of it, and so you should be. Do you go every year?
B: Every year. Take my daughter. She's ten, she loves it.
A: Ten, lovely. My eldest's eleven, she's just starting secondary. Isla. I'm already panicking about her getting a phone. Which is mad, because I deal with it all day at school.
B: Lacey's already on at me. Everyone in her class has got one, apparently.
A: That's what they all say! "Everyone's got one." I hear it fifty times a day. What do you reckon you'll do?
B: Dunno really. Probably give in. My mum'll probably buy her one, she does the pick-ups.
A: Ha, grandparents. Mine are the same. So what's the care home like? Do you enjoy it?
B: Some of it. The residents, some of them. The ladies with dementia, they're lovely. The job itself's badly run. The pay's a joke and the seniors don't do nothing.
A: Yeah. My dad's got carers coming in since his stroke, and honestly, they're the ones that hold it all together. Never get the credit.
B: No, they don't. Nobody thinks about us.
A: Have you thought about moving up? Senior or whatever?
B: Sometimes. Or agency. Or nails from home, I do nails on the side. I just want to stop doing twelves, to be fair.
A: Yeah, twelves sound brutal. I moan about parents' evening and that's till half seven. Sorry, I'm rambling.
B: You're alright. The other two I had didn't really talk much, so.
A: Ha, I'll take that as a compliment. Who'd you have?
B: A student nurse, and a bloke from Notts, Darren, who draws things.
A: Oh, the vinyl man! I thought he looked like a decent bloke for a pint. Was he—
